title: How to Build Better Habits in 4 Simple Steps
coreMove: Diagnose a habit by locating the weak link in cue, craving, response, or reward.
sourcePressure: Habits run through a practical loop of cue, craving, response, and reward, and the Four Laws are direct interventions on that loop.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reducing the habit loop to a memorized diagram rather than a troubleshooting tool.

hook: starting with a definition of cue
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a ferry dispatcher diagnosing why deckhands skip the safety scan
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations lead with a recurring near-miss
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she fixes the cue instead of blaming attention
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she maps cue, craving, response, reward and discovers the scan clipboard is hidden after the rush starts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clipboard wedged behind orange life rings

exampleSpecs.domain: a language learner stuck on evening vocabulary practice
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult learner who assumes she lacks discipline
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the weak link is craving rather than schedule
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she marks cue and response as strong, then pairs the flashcards with a favorite podcast intro to repair craving

exampleSpecs.domain: a veterinary clinic trying to stop missed cage-disinfection steps
exampleSpecs.audience: a head technician seeing infections rise
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether staff identify reward ambiguity rather than training failure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the team adds a visible clean tag so the response has a satisfying endpoint
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stainless kennel door with a blank tag hook

exampleSpecs.domain: a commuter diagnosing why she buys a pastry every train transfer
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who thinks the habit is just hunger
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she separates cue from craving and chooses a new response
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes the loop on the back of her ticket and sees the craving is relief during the seven-minute wait
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a train ticket creased beside a bakery receipt

exampleSpecs.domain: a climbing gym owner increasing waiver completion before belay checks
exampleSpecs.audience: a small-business operator with bottlenecked check-ins
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the habit loop guides redesign instead of nagging
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts response is weak, then sees the real failure is the missing cue before shoe rental
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a waiver tablet dim beside rental climbing shoes

exampleSpecs.domain: a museum conservator establishing a glove-use routine for interns
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a four-step loop prevents fragile prints from being touched barehanded
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places cotton gloves on top of the print box so cue and response sit in the same line of sight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: white gloves resting on a gray archive box

skillTargets: diagnose failed habits by loop component
choose the right Four Laws lever for a scenario
distinguish cue problems from reward problems

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one stuck habit and label its cue, craving, response, and reward. Circle the step that is weakest before changing anything.
